goal: Make the Azure DevOps build restore the win-x64 runtime packs needed by the .NET 8 Windows desktop/MSIX build.
must_include: Identifies NETSDK1112 as a restore/build mismatch for the `win-x64` runtime packs, not a missing .NET SDK installation.

Changes the project from singular `<RuntimeIdentifier>win-x64</RuntimeIdentifier>` to `<RuntimeIdentifiers>win-x64</RuntimeIdentifiers>` or otherwise ensures restore is performed with `win-x64` before the VSBuild step.
Keeps the pipeline build platform aligned with the RID, for example `platform: x64` with `win-x64`.
Adds or verifies an explicit restore step that runs after `UseDotNet@2` and before building if the pipeline does not rely on VSBuild restore.
must_not: Tell them to install a desktop runtime manually on the hosted agent as the fix.
Downgrade the project back to .NET 7 without addressing RID restore.
Clear NuGet caches or retry the pipeline as the main solution.
acceptable_alternatives: `msbuild /restore /p:RuntimeIdentifier=win-x64` with the same configuration and platform used for packaging.
Publish self-contained with `-r win-x64` when that matches the app's deployment plan.
solved: The CI restore downloads `Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64` and `Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x64`, and the .NET 8 package build proceeds past NETSDK1112.
partial: The answer says to restore for win-x64 but does not update the project or pipeline so restore and build use the same RID/platform.
notes: The accepted Stack Overflow answer fixes this repro by using `RuntimeIdentifiers` so restore includes the runtime pack.
